segments.title: Foreign interference — Hogue and NSICOP
segments.narration: Intelligence leaks, NSICOP reporting, and the Hogue Commission put PRC and other state interference into the public square. Diaspora intimidation and electoral integrity become permanent files. The film maps named processes without turning diaspora communities into suspects.

segments.title: Media concentration and public subsidy stack
segments.narration: Ownership concentration, Meta news blocks, and federal media supports reshape the information environment. CBC appropriations and Online News Act fights sit beside independent outlets. The five-generation warfare frame treats brand legitimacy as a strategic asset.

segments.title: Defence procurement — CSC, ships, and capability lag
segments.narration: Canadian Surface Combatant cost trajectories, recruitment crisis, and Arctic capability gaps enter AG and parliamentary scrutiny. The later Griffon GLLE pause is a continuation, not a novelty.

segments.title: Opioid crisis — toxic supply and accountability
segments.narration: Death counts mount under a toxic drug supply. Provincial experiments diverge. Federal-provincial blame cycles dominate. Public health data and coroner series are the primary instruments — not culture-war slogans alone.

segments.title: Veterans and MAID offers — documented cases
segments.narration: Parliamentary testimony and reporting document cases where veterans seeking assistance were directed toward MAID pathways. These are among the most severe legitimacy shocks in the modern social compact — preserved as primary case files on this site.

segments.title: Carbon pricing politics and cost-of-living collision
segments.narration: Federal carbon pricing becomes a central electoral and regional cleavage while inflation and housing stress peak. The film tracks statute and rebate design against public affordability metrics without collapsing into campaign ads.

segments.title: Online harms bills — speech and platform power
segments.narration: Successive online harms proposals raise questions about state power over digital speech, platform liability, and due process. Primary sources: bill texts, committee briefs, charter analyses — not only influencer panic.

segments.title: Hogue Commission — foreign interference
segments.narration: The Hogue Commission and NSICOP document foreign interference, naming the People's Republic of China as principal state actor and describing parliamentarians under foreign influence. Enforcement lags findings. That gap is the story.

segments.title: Media funding and concentration
